title.zh: 卷五十三 志第二十九 禮七
title.raw: 卷五十三 志第二十九 禮七 Volume 53 Treatises 29: Rites 7

sentences.zh: 嘉禮一

translations.literal: Auspicious Rites One
translations.idiomatic: Part One: Auspicious Rites

sentences.zh: 登極儀 大朝儀 常朝儀 皇太子親王朝儀 諸王來朝儀 諸司朝覲儀 中宮受朝儀 朝賀東宮儀 大宴儀 上尊號徽號儀

translations.literal: Enthronement Rite, Grand Audience Rite, Regular Audience Rite, Crown Prince's Personal Audience Rite, Princes' Coming-to-Court Rite, Various Offices' Audience Rite, Inner Palace Reception Rite, Eastern Palace Congratulations Rite, Grand Banquet Rite, Bestowal of Honorific Title Rite
translations.idiomatic: Enthronement; Grand Audience; Regular Audience; Crown Prince's Personal Audience; Princes' Coming to Court; Various Offices' Audience; Inner Palace Reception; Congratulations at the Eastern Palace; Grand Banquet; Bestowal of Honorific Titles

sentences.zh: 二曰嘉禮。

translations.literal: The second is called Auspicious Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The second category of rites is the Auspicious Rites.

sentences.zh: 行於朝廷者，曰朝會，曰宴饗，曰上尊號、徽號，曰冊命，曰經筵，曰表箋。

translations.literal: Those performed at court are called court assembly, banquet feast, bestowing honorific titles and honorific epithets, investiture edicts, imperial lecture, and memorials and petitions.
translations.idiomatic: Those performed at court include court assemblies, banquets, the bestowal of honorific titles and epithets, investiture edicts, the imperial lecture, and the presentation of memorials and petitions.

sentences.zh: 行於辟雍者，曰視學。

translations.literal: Those performed at the Imperial Academy are called inspecting study.
translations.idiomatic: Those performed at the Imperial Academy are known as the inspection of learning.

sentences.zh: 自天子達於庶人者，曰冠，曰婚。

translations.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to commoners are called capping and marriage.
translations.idiomatic: From the Son of Heaven down to commoners, these are the capping ceremony and marriage.

sentences.zh: 行於天下者，曰巡狩，曰詔赦，曰鄉飲酒。

translations.literal: Those performed throughout the realm are called imperial tour, amnesty edicts, and village drinking ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Those performed throughout the realm include the imperial tour, amnesty edicts, and the village drinking ceremony.

sentences.zh: 舉其大者書之。

translations.literal: The major ones are recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Only the major ceremonies are recorded here.

sentences.zh: 儀之同者，則各附於其類云。

translations.literal: Ceremonies that are alike are each attached to their category.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonies that share the same form are grouped under their respective categories.

sentences.zh: 登極儀

translations.literal: Enthronement Rite
translations.idiomatic: The Enthronement Rite

sentences.zh: 即位日，先告祀天地。

translations.literal: On the day of accession, first report and sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of accession, the emperor first announces the event and offers sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 禮成，即帝位於南郊。

translations.literal: When the rite is complete, assume the imperial throne at the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite is finished, he assumes the imperial throne at the Southern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 丞相率百官以下及都民耆老，拜賀舞蹈，呼萬歲者三。

translations.literal: The chancellor leads all officials below him and the capital's elderly populace in bowing congratulations and ritual dance, calling "ten thousand years" three times.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor leads all officials and the capital's elderly residents in bowing, offering congratulations, and performing the ritual dance, shouting "Long live the emperor!" three times.

sentences.zh: 具鹵簿導從，詣太廟，上追尊四世冊寶，告祀社稷。

translations.literal: Complete with imperial escort guard, proceed to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, present posthumous honorific titles and seals for four generations, and announce sacrifices at the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanied by the full imperial escort, he proceeds to the Imperial Ancestral Temple to bestow posthumous honorific titles and seals upon four generations of ancestors, then announces sacrifices at the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 還，具袞冕，御奉天殿，百官上表賀。

translations.literal: Return, don full imperial regalia, ascend the Hall of Supreme Harmony, all officials present memorials of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Upon returning, he dons full imperial regalia and takes his seat in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, where all officials present memorials of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 先期，侍儀司設表案于丹墀內道之西北，設丞相以下拜位於內道東西，每等異位，重行北面。

translations.literal: In advance, the Ceremonial Service sets the memorial table in the northwest of the inner path of the red steps, and sets bowing positions for the chancellor and below on the east and west of the inner path, each rank in a separate position, double rows facing north.
translations.idiomatic: In advance, the Ceremonial Service places the memorial table in the northwest corner of the inner path on the red steps, and arranges bowing positions for the chancellor and all officials below him along the east and west sides of the inner path, with each rank in its own place in double rows facing north.

sentences.zh: 捧表、展表、宣表官位於表案西，東向。

translations.literal: The officials who present, unfold, and proclaim the memorial stand west of the memorial table, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The officials who present, unfold, and proclaim the memorial stand to the west of the memorial table, facing east.

sentences.zh: 糾儀御史二人於表案南，東西向。

translations.literal: Two censorial officials for correcting ritual stand south of the memorial table, one facing east and one facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Two censorial officials charged with correcting ritual deportment stand south of the memorial table, one facing east and one facing west.

sentences.zh: 宿衛鎮撫二人於東西陛下，護衛百戶二十四人於其南，稍後。

translations.literal: Two garrison commanders on the east and west stairways, twenty-four guard company commanders south of them, slightly to the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Two garrison commanders stand on the east and west stairways, with twenty-four guard company commanders positioned to their south, slightly to the rear.

sentences.zh: 知班二人，於文武官拜位北，東西向。

translations.literal: Two officials who know the ranks stand north of the civil and military officials' bowing positions, one facing east and one facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Two officials who direct the ranks stand north of the civil and military officials' bowing positions, one facing east and one facing west.

sentences.zh: 通贊、贊禮二人於知班北，通贊西，贊禮東。

translations.literal: The general announcer and ritual announcer, two persons, north of the rank directors; the general announcer on the west, the ritual announcer on the east.
translations.idiomatic: The general announcer and the ritual announcer stand north of the rank directors, with the general announcer on the west and the ritual announcer on the east.

sentences.zh: 引文武班四人於文武官拜位北，稍後，東西向。

translations.literal: Four ushers for the civil and military ranks north of the civil and military officials' bowing positions, slightly to the rear, one facing east and one facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Four ushers for the civil and military ranks stand north of the officials' bowing positions, slightly to the rear, one pair facing east and one facing west.

sentences.zh: 引殿前班二人於引文武班南。

translations.literal: Two ushers for the hall-front rank south of the civil and military rank ushers.
translations.idiomatic: Two ushers for the hall-front rank stand south of the civil and military rank ushers.

sentences.zh: 舉表案二人於引文武班北。

translations.literal: Two officials who raise the memorial table north of the civil and military rank ushers.
translations.idiomatic: Two officials who carry the memorial table stand north of the civil and military rank ushers.

sentences.zh: 舉殿上表案二人於西陛下，東向。

translations.literal: Two officials who raise the hall memorial table on the west stairway, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Two officials who carry the hall memorial table stand on the west stairway, facing east.

sentences.zh: 丹陛上設殿前班指揮司官三人，東向。

translations.literal: On the red steps are set three commandery officials of the hall-front rank, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: On the red steps, three commandery officials of the hall-front rank are positioned, facing east.

sentences.zh: 宣徽院官三人，西向。

translations.literal: Three officials of the Xuanhui Court, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Three officials of the Xuanhui Court stand facing west.

sentences.zh: 儀鸞司官於殿中門之左右，護衛千戶八人於殿東西門，俱東西向。

translations.literal: Officials of the Ceremonial Guard on the left and right of the central hall gate, eight guard battalion commanders at the east and west hall gates, all facing east or west.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Ceremonial Guard stand to the left and right of the central hall gate, and eight guard battalion commanders are posted at the east and west hall gates, all facing east or west.

sentences.zh: 鳴鞭四人於殿前班之南，北向。

translations.literal: Four whip-crackers south of the hall-front rank, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Four whip-crackers stand south of the hall-front rank, facing north.

sentences.zh: 將軍六人於殿門左右，天武將軍四人於陛上四隅，俱東西向。

translations.literal: Six generals on the left and right of the hall gate, four celestial martial generals at the four corners of the steps, all facing east or west.
translations.idiomatic: Six generals stand on either side of the hall gate, and four celestial martial generals are posted at the four corners of the steps, all facing east or west.

sentences.zh: 殿上，尚寶司設寶案於正中，侍儀司設表案於寶案南。

translations.literal: In the hall, the Imperial Seals Office sets the seal table in the center, the Ceremonial Service sets the memorial table south of the seal table.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the hall, the Imperial Seals Office places the seal table at the center, and the Ceremonial Service places the memorial table to its south.

sentences.zh: 文武侍從兩班於殿上東西，文起居注、給事中、殿中侍御史、尚寶卿，武懸刀指揮，東西向。

translations.literal: Civil and military attendant ranks in two columns on the east and west of the hall: civil—diarist, supervising secretary, palace censor, director of imperial seals; military—saber-bearing commanders; all facing east or west.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military attendants are arranged in two columns on the east and west sides of the hall: on the civil side, the diarist, supervising secretary, palace censor, and director of imperial seals; on the military side, the saber-bearing commanders—all facing east or west.

sentences.zh: 受表官於文侍從班南，西向。

translations.literal: The official who receives the memorial south of the civil attendant rank, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The official who receives the memorial stands south of the civil attendant column, facing west.

sentences.zh: 內贊二人於受表官之南，捲簾將軍二人簾前，俱東西向。

translations.literal: Two inner announcers south of the memorial-receiving official, two curtain-rolling generals before the curtain, all facing east or west.
translations.idiomatic: Two inner announcers stand south of the memorial-receiving official, and two curtain-rolling generals are posted before the curtain, all facing east or west.

sentences.zh: 是日，拱衛司陳鹵簿，列甲士於午門外，列旗仗，設五輅於奉天門外，侍儀舍人二，舉表案入。

translations.literal: On that day, the Imperial Guard displays the ceremonial escort, arrays armored soldiers outside the Meridian Gate, arrays flags and regalia, sets the five imperial carriages outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, two ceremonial attendants carry the memorial table in.
translations.idiomatic: On that day, the Imperial Guard displays the full ceremonial escort, arrays armored soldiers outside the Meridian Gate, lines up flags and regalia, sets out the five imperial carriages outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, and two ceremonial attendants carry the memorial table inside.

sentences.zh: 鼓初嚴，百官朝服立午門外。

translations.literal: At the first drum signal, all officials in court dress stand outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the first drum signal, all officials in court dress take their places outside the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 通贊、贊禮、宿衛官、諸侍衛及尚寶卿侍從官入。

translations.literal: The general announcer, ritual announcer, garrison officials, various guards, and attendant officials including the director of imperial seals enter.
translations.idiomatic: The general announcer, ritual announcer, garrison officials, various guards, and attendant officials including the director of imperial seals enter the hall.

sentences.zh: 鼓三嚴，丞相以下入。

translations.literal: At the third drum signal, the chancellor and those below enter.
translations.idiomatic: At the third drum signal, the chancellor and all officials below him enter.

sentences.zh: 皇帝袞冕升御座，大樂鼓吹振作。

translations.literal: The emperor in full regalia ascends the imperial throne, great music and wind instruments strike up.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, dressed in full regalia, ascends the imperial throne as great music and wind instruments strike up.

sentences.zh: 樂止，將軍捲簾，尚寶卿置寶於案。

translations.literal: Music stops, the general rolls up the curtain, the director of imperial seals places the seal on the table.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceases, the general rolls up the curtain, and the director of imperial seals places the imperial seal on the table.

sentences.zh: 拱衛司鳴鞭，引班導百官入丹墀拜位。

translations.literal: The Imperial Guard cracks the whip, the rank ushers lead all officials into the red-courtyard bowing positions.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Guard cracks the whip, and the rank ushers lead all officials to their bowing positions on the red courtyard.

sentences.zh: 初行樂作，至位樂止。

translations.literal: At the first movement music plays, upon reaching position music stops.
translations.idiomatic: Music plays as they begin to move, and ceases once they reach their positions.

sentences.zh: 知班贊班，贊禮贊拜。

translations.literal: The rank director announces the ranks, the ritual announcer announces the bow.
translations.idiomatic: The rank director calls the ranks to order, and the ritual announcer announces the bow.

sentences.zh: 樂作，四拜，興。

translations.literal: Music plays, four bows, rise.
translations.idiomatic: Music plays; they perform four bows and rise.

sentences.zh: 樂止。

translations.literal: Music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceases.

sentences.zh: 捧表以下官由殿西門入。

translations.literal: The memorial-presenting officials and those below enter through the west hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial-presenting officials and those assisting them enter through the west hall gate.

sentences.zh: 內贊贊進表。

translations.literal: The inner announcer announces presenting the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The inner announcer announces the presentation of the memorial.

sentences.zh: 捧表官跪捧。

translations.literal: The memorial-presenting official kneels and presents it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial-presenting official kneels and holds up the memorial.

sentences.zh: 受表官搢笏，跪受，置於案。

translations.literal: The memorial-receiving official inserts his tablet, kneels to receive it, and places it on the table.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial-receiving official inserts his tablet, kneels to receive the memorial, and places it on the table.

sentences.zh: 出笏，興，退立，東向。

translations.literal: Withdraws the tablet, rises, withdraws and stands, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: He withdraws his tablet, rises, steps back, and stands facing east.

sentences.zh: 內贊贊宣表。

translations.literal: The inner announcer announces proclaiming the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The inner announcer announces the proclamation of the memorial.

sentences.zh: 宣表官前，搢笏，跪，展表官搢笏，同跪。

translations.literal: The memorial-proclaiming official advances, inserts his tablet, kneels; the memorial-unfolding official inserts his tablet and kneels together.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial-proclaiming official steps forward, inserts his tablet, and kneels; the memorial-unfolding official inserts his tablet and kneels beside him.

sentences.zh: 宣訖，展表官出笏，以表復於案，俱退。

translations.literal: When proclamation is finished, the unfolding official withdraws his tablet, returns the memorial to the table, both withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation is finished, the unfolding official withdraws his tablet, returns the memorial to the table, and both withdraw.

sentences.zh: 宣表官俯伏興。

translations.literal: The proclaiming official prostrates and rises.
translations.idiomatic: The proclaiming official prostrates himself and then rises.

sentences.zh: 俱出殿西門，復位。

translations.literal: All exit through the west hall gate and return to their positions.
translations.idiomatic: They all exit through the west hall gate and return to their positions.

sentences.zh: 贊禮贊拜。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer announces the bow.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer announces the bow.

sentences.zh: 樂作，四拜，樂止。

translations.literal: Music plays, four bows, music stops.
translations.idiomatic: Music plays; they perform four bows, and the music ceases.

sentences.zh: 搢笏，鞠躬三，舞蹈。

translations.literal: Insert tablets, bow three times, perform ritual dance.
translations.idiomatic: They insert their tablets, bow three times, and perform the ritual dance.

sentences.zh: 拱手加額，呼萬歲者三。

translations.literal: Cup hands and touch forehead, call "ten thousand years" three times.
translations.idiomatic: They cup their hands and touch their foreheads, shouting "Long live the emperor!" three times.

sentences.zh: 出笏，俯伏興。

translations.literal: Withdraw tablets, prostrate and rise.
translations.idiomatic: They withdraw their tablets, prostrate themselves, and rise.

sentences.zh: 樂作，四拜，賀畢。

translations.literal: Music plays, four bows, congratulations finished.
translations.idiomatic: Music plays; they perform four final bows, and the congratulations are complete.

sentences.zh: 遂遣官冊拜皇后，冊立皇太子，以即位詔告天下。

translations.literal: Then dispatch officials to invest the empress with a seal, invest the crown prince, and announce the accession edict to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then dispatches officials to invest the empress and crown prince by edict, and proclaims the accession edict to the realm.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位倉猝，其議不詳。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor acceded, it was hasty, and the deliberations are not detailed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor's accession was hurried, and the deliberations on its rites are not recorded in detail.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，先期，司設監陳御座於奉天門，欽天監設定時鼓，尚寶司設寶案，教坊司設中和韶樂，設而不作。

translations.literal: When the Hongxi Emperor acceded, in advance the Directorate of Palace Equipment displayed the imperial throne at the Gate of Supreme Harmony, the Directorate of Astronomy set the timekeeping drums, the Imperial Seals Office set the seal table, the Music Office set the Harmonious Imperial Music, set up but not played.
translations.idiomatic: For the Hongxi Emperor's accession, the Directorate of Palace Equipment placed the imperial throne at the Gate of Supreme Harmony in advance; the Directorate of Astronomy set the timekeeping drums; the Imperial Seals Office prepared the seal table; and the Music Office set out the Harmonious Imperial Music—but did not play it.

sentences.zh: 是日早，遣官告天地宗社，皇帝具孝服告几筵。

translations.literal: Early that day, dispatch officials to announce to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral altars; the emperor in mourning dress announces at the spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Early that morning, officials were dispatched to announce the accession to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral altars, while the emperor in mourning dress made his announcement before the deceased emperor's spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 至時，鳴鐘鼓，設鹵簿。

translations.literal: At the appointed time, bells and drums sound, the ceremonial escort is set out.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed hour, bells and drums sounded and the full ceremonial escort was deployed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝袞冕，御奉天門。

translations.literal: The emperor in full regalia takes his seat at the Gate of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, dressed in full regalia, took his seat at the Gate of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 百官朝服，入午門。

translations.literal: All officials in court dress enter the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: All officials in court dress entered through the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚寺導執事官行禮，請升御座。

translations.literal: The Court of State Ceremonial leads the officiating officials in performing the rite and requests ascending the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of State Ceremonial led the officiating officials through the rites and requested that the emperor ascend the throne.

sentences.zh: 皇帝由中門出。

translations.literal: The emperor exits through the central gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor emerged through the central gate.

sentences.zh: 升座，鳴鞭。

translations.literal: Ascends the throne, the whip is cracked.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended the throne, and the whip was cracked.

sentences.zh: 百官上表，行禮，頒詔，俱如儀。

translations.literal: All officials present memorials, perform the rite, promulgate the edict, all according to the prescribed ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The officials presented their memorials, performed the prescribed rites, and the accession edict was promulgated—all according to established ceremony.

sentences.zh: 宣宗以後，儲宮嗣立者並同。

translations.literal: From the Xuande Emperor onward, those who succeeded from the Eastern Palace all followed the same procedure.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xuande Emperor onward, heirs apparent who succeeded to the throne followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年，世宗入承大統。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhengde, the Jiajing Emperor entered to succeed the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of the Zhengde reign, the Jiajing Emperor entered the capital to succeed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 先期造行殿於宣武門外，南向。

translations.literal: In advance construct a traveling hall outside the Xuanwu Gate, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: A traveling hall was constructed in advance outside the Xuanwu Gate, facing south.

sentences.zh: 設帷幄御座，備翼善冠服及鹵簿大駕以候。

translations.literal: Set up curtained imperial throne, prepare the Yishan crown and robes and the full ceremonial escort and grand carriage to await.
translations.idiomatic: A curtained imperial throne was set up, along with the Yishan crown and robes and the full ceremonial escort and grand carriage, all prepared in waiting.

sentences.zh: 至期，百官郊迎。

translations.literal: When the day arrived, all officials welcomed him at the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, all officials went out to the suburbs to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 駕入行殿，行四拜禮。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage enters the traveling hall, performs the four-bow rite.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage entered the traveling hall, where the four-bow rite was performed.

sentences.zh: 明日，由大明門入。

translations.literal: The next day, enter through the Gate of Great Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: The following day, he entered through the Gate of Great Brightness.

sentences.zh: 省詔草，改年號，素服詣大行几筵謁告。

translations.literal: Review the draft edict, change the reign title, in plain robes proceed to the deceased emperor's spirit tablet to announce.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed the draft edict, changed the reign title, and in plain robes went to announce before the deceased emperor's spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 畢，設香案奉天殿丹陛上。

translations.literal: When finished, set an incense table on the red steps of the Hall of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: When this was finished, an incense table was set on the red steps of the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 皇帝袞冕，行告天地禮。

translations.literal: The emperor in full regalia performs the rite of announcing to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, dressed in full regalia, performed the rite of announcing his accession to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 詣奉先殿、奉慈殿謁告，仍詣大行几筵、慈壽皇太后、莊肅皇后前各行禮，遂御華蓋殿。

translations.literal: Proceed to the Hall of Imperial Ancestors and Hall of Imperial Consorts to announce, still proceed before the deceased emperor's spirit tablet, the Empress Dowager Cishou, and Empress Zhuangsu to perform rites at each, then take seat at the Hall of Imperial Canopy.
translations.idiomatic: He proceeded to the Hall of Imperial Ancestors and the Hall of Imperial Consorts to make his announcements, then performed rites before the deceased emperor's spirit tablet, before Empress Dowager Cishou, and before Empress Zhuangsu in turn, and then took his seat in the Hall of Imperial Canopy.

sentences.zh: 百官朝服入。

translations.literal: All officials in court dress enter.
translations.idiomatic: All officials entered in court dress.

sentences.zh: 傳旨免賀，五拜三稽首。

translations.literal: An edict is transmitted exempting congratulations, five bows and three prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was transmitted exempting full congratulations; the officials performed five bows and three prostrations instead.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚寺官請升殿，帝由中門出御奉天殿。

translations.literal: An official of the Court of State Ceremonial requests ascending the hall; the emperor exits through the central gate and takes his seat at the Hall of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: An official of the Court of State Ceremonial requested that the emperor ascend the hall; the emperor emerged through the central gate and took his seat in the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 鳴鞭，贊拜，頒詔，如制。

translations.literal: Crack the whip, announce the bow, promulgate the edict, as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: The whip was cracked, the bows were announced, and the edict was promulgated—all as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 大朝儀

translations.literal: Grand Audience Rite
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Audience Rite

sentences.zh: 漢正會禮，夜漏未盡七刻，鐘鳴受賀。

translations.literal: The Han New Year's assembly rite: before the night water-clock has run seven marks, the bell sounds and congratulations are received.
translations.idiomatic: In the Han dynasty's New Year's assembly rite, before the night water-clock had run seven marks, the bell sounded and the emperor received congratulations.

sentences.zh: 公卿以下執贄來庭，二千石以上升殿，稱萬歲，然後宴饗。

translations.literal: Dukes and ministers and below bearing gifts come to the court, those of two-thousand-bushel rank and above ascend the hall, call "ten thousand years," then the banquet feast.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, ministers, and officials below them came to court bearing gifts; those of two-thousand-bushel rank and above ascended the hall, shouted "Long live the emperor!", and only then was the banquet held.

sentences.zh: 晉《咸寧注》，有晨賀晝會之分。

translations.literal: The Jin dynasty's Xianning Commentary distinguishes morning congratulations from daytime assembly.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin dynasty's Xianning Commentary distinguishes between morning congratulations and the daytime assembly.

sentences.zh: 唐制，正旦、冬至、五月朔、千秋節，咸受朝賀。

translations.literal: The Tang system: New Year's Day, winter solstice, first day of the fifth month, and the Longevity Festival—all received court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang system, the emperor received court congratulations on New Year's Day, the winter solstice, the first day of the fifth month, and the Longevity Festival.

sentences.zh: 宋因之。

translations.literal: The Song followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Song dynasty followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 明太祖洪武元年九月，定正旦朝會儀，與登極略相仿。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Hongwu under the Ming founder, the New Year's court assembly rite was established, broadly similar to the enthronement rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of the Hongwu reign, the Ming founder established the New Year's court assembly rite, which broadly resembled the enthronement rite.

sentences.zh: 其後屢詔更定，立爲中制。

translations.literal: Afterward repeatedly ordered to be revised and established as the standard middle regulations.
translations.idiomatic: It was subsequently revised by imperial edict on several occasions and established as the standard middle regulations.

sentences.zh: 凡正旦冬至，先日，尚寶司設御座於奉天殿，及寶案於御座東，香案于丹陛南。

translations.literal: For all New Year's Days and winter solstices, the day before, the Imperial Seals Office sets the imperial throne in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, and the seal table east of the throne, an incense table south on the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: For every New Year's Day and winter solstice, on the day before, the Imperial Seals Office places the imperial throne in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, the seal table to its east, and an incense table on the southern red steps.

sentences.zh: 教坊司設中和韶樂於殿內東西，北向。

translations.literal: The Music Office sets the Harmonious Imperial Music on the east and west inside the hall, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Office positions the Harmonious Imperial Music ensemble on the east and west sides inside the hall, facing north.

sentences.zh: 翌明，錦衣衛陳鹵簿、儀仗于丹陛及丹墀，設明扇於殿內，列車輅于丹墀。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, the Embroidered Uniform Guard displays the ceremonial escort and regalia on the red steps and red courtyard, sets bright fans inside the hall, arrays the imperial carriages on the red courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the following day, the Embroidered Uniform Guard displays the ceremonial escort and regalia on the red steps and red courtyard, sets out the bright fans inside the hall, and lines up the imperial carriages on the red courtyard.

sentences.zh: 鳴鞭四人，左右北向。

translations.literal: Four whip-crackers, left and right facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Four whip-crackers are posted on the left and right, facing north.

sentences.zh: 教坊司陳大樂於丹陛東西，北向，儀禮司設同文、玉帛兩案于丹陛東。

translations.literal: The Music Office displays great music on the east and west of the red steps, facing north; the Ceremonial Protocol Office sets the Shared Script and Jade-Silk tables on the east of the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Office sets out the great music ensemble on the east and west sides of the red steps, facing north, while the Ceremonial Protocol Office places the Shared Script and Jade-Silk tables on the eastern red steps.

sentences.zh: 金吾衛設護衛官於殿內及丹陛，陳甲士于丹墀至午門外，錦衣衛設將軍于丹陛至奉天門外，陳旗幟於奉天門外，俱東西列。

translations.literal: The Golden Guard sets guard officials inside the hall and on the red steps, arrays armored soldiers from the red courtyard to outside the Meridian Gate; the Embroidered Uniform Guard sets generals from the red steps to outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, arrays flags and banners outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, all arrayed east and west.
translations.idiomatic: The Golden Guard posted guard officials inside the hall and on the red steps, and arrayed armored soldiers from the red courtyard to outside the Meridian Gate; the Embroidered Uniform Guard posted generals from the red steps to outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony and lined up flags and banners outside that gate—all in east-west columns.

sentences.zh: 典牧所陳仗馬犀象於文、武樓南，東西向。

translations.literal: The Imperial Herds Office displays ceremonial horses, rhinoceroses, and elephants south of the Civil and Military Towers, facing east or west.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Herds Office displayed ceremonial horses, rhinoceroses, and elephants south of the Civil and Military Towers, facing east or west.

sentences.zh: 司晨郎報時位於內道東，近北。

translations.literal: The dawn herald who announces the time stands on the east of the inner path, near the north.
translations.idiomatic: The dawn herald who announced the time stood on the east side of the inner path, near its northern end.

sentences.zh: 糾儀御史二，位於丹墀北，內贊二，位於殿內，外贊二，位於丹墀北，傳制、宣表等官位於殿內，俱東西向。

translations.literal: Two censorial officials for correcting ritual north of the red courtyard; two inner announcers inside the hall; two outer announcers north of the red courtyard; edict-transmitting, memorial-proclaiming, and other officials inside the hall, all facing east or west.
translations.idiomatic: Two censorial officials charged with correcting ritual deportment stood north of the red courtyard; two inner announcers were inside the hall; two outer announcers stood north of the red courtyard; and officials who transmitted edicts, proclaimed memorials, and the like were inside the hall—all facing east or west.

sentences.zh: 鼓初嚴，百官朝服，班午門外。

translations.literal: At the first drum signal, all officials in court dress form ranks outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the first drum signal, all officials in court dress formed ranks outside the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 次嚴，由左、右掖門入，詣丹墀東西，北向立。

translations.literal: At the second signal, enter through the left and right side gates, proceed to the east and west of the red courtyard, stand facing north.
translations.idiomatic: At the second signal, they entered through the left and right side gates, took their places on the east and west sides of the red courtyard, and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 三嚴，執事官詣華蓋殿，帝具袞冕升座，鐘聲止。

translations.literal: At the third signal, officiating officials proceed to the Hall of Imperial Canopy; the emperor in full regalia ascends the throne; the bell sounds cease.
translations.idiomatic: At the third signal, the officiating officials proceeded to the Hall of Imperial Canopy, where the emperor in full regalia ascended the throne and the bell sounds ceased.

sentences.zh: 儀禮司奏執事官行禮，贊五拜，畢，奏請升殿。

translations.literal: The Ceremonial Protocol Office reports that officiating officials perform the rite, announces five bows, when finished reports requesting ascending the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonial Protocol Office announced that the officiating officials should perform the rite; five bows were announced, and when these were finished, it was reported that the emperor should ascend the hall.

sentences.zh: 駕興，中和樂作。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage rises, the Harmonious Music plays.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage set out, and the Harmonious Music began to play.

sentences.zh: 尚寶司捧寶前行，導駕官前導，扇開簾卷，寶置於案，樂止。

translations.literal: The Imperial Seals Office bears the seal forward, guiding officials lead ahead, fans open and curtain rolls up, the seal is placed on the table, music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Seals Office bore the seal forward as guiding officials led the way; the fans opened, the curtain was rolled up, the seal was placed on the table, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 鳴鞭報時，對贊唱排班，班齊。

translations.literal: Crack the whip and announce the time, the paired announcers call forming ranks, ranks aligned.
translations.idiomatic: The whip was cracked and the time announced; the paired announcers called the officials to form ranks until all were aligned.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱鞠躬，大樂作。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer calls bowing, great music plays.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer called for bows, and great music began to play.

sentences.zh: 贊四拜，興，樂上。

translations.literal: Announce four bows, rise, music ascends.
translations.idiomatic: Four bows were announced; the officials rose as the music swelled.

sentences.zh: 典儀唱進表，樂作。

translations.literal: The ceremonial director calls presenting the memorial, music plays.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial director announced the presentation of the memorial, and music played.

sentences.zh: 給事中二人，詣同文案前，導引序班舉案由東門入，置殿中，樂止。

translations.literal: Two supervising secretaries proceed before the Shared Script table, ushers of the rank order raise the table and enter through the east gate, place it in the hall, music stops.
translations.idiomatic: Two supervising secretaries proceeded before the Shared Script table; rank-order ushers raised the memorial table, entered through the east gate, placed it in the hall, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 內贊唱宣表目。

translations.literal: The inner announcer calls proclaiming the memorial heading.
translations.idiomatic: The inner announcer announced the proclamation of the memorial heading.

sentences.zh: 宣表目官跪，宣訖，俯伏，興。

translations.literal: The heading-proclaiming official kneels, when proclamation is finished prostrates and rises.
translations.idiomatic: The official who proclaimed the memorial heading knelt, and when the proclamation was finished, prostrated himself and rose.

sentences.zh: 唱宣表，展表官取表，宣表官至簾前，外贊唱，衆官皆跪。

translations.literal: Call proclaiming the memorial; the unfolding official takes the memorial; the proclaiming official reaches before the curtain; the outer announcer calls; all officials kneel.
translations.idiomatic: The proclamation of the memorial was announced; the unfolding official took up the memorial; the proclaiming official advanced to the curtain; the outer announcer called out, and all officials knelt.

sentences.zh: 宣表訖，內外皆唱，俯伏，興。

translations.literal: When proclamation is finished, inner and outer announcers both call; prostrate and rise.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation was finished, both inner and outer announcers called out; the officials prostrated themselves and rose.

sentences.zh: 序班舉表案於殿東，外贊唱衆官皆跪。

translations.literal: The rank-order ushers raise the memorial table on the east of the hall; the outer announcer calls all officials kneel.
translations.idiomatic: The rank-order ushers raised the memorial table on the east side of the hall, and the outer announcer called for all officials to kneel.

sentences.zh: 代致詞官跪丹陛中，致詞云： 「具官臣某，茲遇正旦，三陽開泰，萬物鹹新。

translations.literal: The substitute speech-offering official kneels in the center of the red steps and offers the speech, saying: "Your servant official So-and-so, on this occasion of New Year's Day, the three yangs open prosperity, all things are newly renewed."
translations.idiomatic: The substitute speech-offering official knelt in the center of the red steps and delivered the congratulatory address: "Your servant official So-and-so, on this New Year's Day, as the three yang forces open the season of renewal, all things are made new."

sentences.zh: 」冬至則云：「律應黃種，日當長至。

translations.literal: " For the winter solstice it says: "The pitch-pipe responds to the yellow bell seed, the day is at the utmost lengthening."
translations.idiomatic: " For the winter solstice it says: "The pitch-pipe responds to the yellow bell seed, and the day has reached its utmost lengthening."

sentences.zh: 」「恭惟皇帝陛下，膺乾納祜，奉天永昌。

translations.literal: " "Respectfully considering Your Majesty the Emperor, receiving Heaven's mandate and accepting blessings, upholding Heaven's eternal prosperity."
translations.idiomatic: " "We respectfully consider that Your Majesty the Emperor has received Heaven's mandate and accepted its blessings, and upholds Heaven's eternal prosperity."

sentences.zh: 」賀畢，外贊唱，衆官皆俯伏，興。

translations.literal: " When congratulations are finished, the outer announcer calls; all officials prostrate and rise.
translations.idiomatic: " When the congratulations were finished, the outer announcer called out, and all officials prostrated themselves and rose.

sentences.zh: 樂作，四拜，興。

translations.literal: Music plays, four bows, rise.
translations.idiomatic: Music played; they performed four bows and rose.

sentences.zh: 樂止。

translations.literal: Music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceased.

sentences.zh: 傳制官跪奏傳制，由東門出，至丹陛，東向立，稱有制。

translations.literal: The edict-transmitting official kneels and reports transmitting the edict, exits through the east gate, reaches the red steps, stands facing east, and declares "There is an edict."
translations.idiomatic: The edict-transmitting official knelt and reported that he would transmit the edict, then exited through the east gate, came to the red steps, stood facing east, and declared, "There is an edict."

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱，跪，宣制。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer calls kneel and proclaim the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer called for them to kneel and proclaimed the edict.

sentences.zh: 正旦則云：「履端之慶，與卿等同之。

translations.literal: For New Year's Day it says: "The celebration of treading the beginning, I share it with you all."
translations.idiomatic: For New Year's Day it says: "The celebration of the year's beginning—I share it with you all."

sentences.zh: 」冬至則云：「履長之慶，與卿等同之。

translations.literal: " For the winter solstice it says: "The celebration of treading the lengthening, I share it with you all."
translations.idiomatic: " For the winter solstice it says: "The celebration of the year's lengthening—I share it with you all."

sentences.zh: 」萬壽聖節則致詞曰：「具官臣某，欽遇皇帝陛下聖誕之辰，謹率文武官僚敬祝萬歲壽。

translations.literal: " For the Longevity Sacred Festival the speech says: "Your servant official So-and-so, reverently on the occasion of Your Majesty the Emperor's sacred birthday, respectfully leads civil and military officials in respectfully wishing ten thousand years of life."
translations.idiomatic: " For the Longevity Sacred Festival the address says: "Your servant official So-and-so, on this sacred birthday of Your Majesty the Emperor, respectfully leads the civil and military officials in wishing you ten thousand years of life."

sentences.zh: 」不傳制。

translations.literal: " No edict is transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: " No edict was transmitted on this occasion.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱俯伏，興。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer calls prostrate and rise.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer called for them to prostrate themselves and rise.

sentences.zh: 樂止。

translations.literal: Music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceased.

sentences.zh: 贊搢笏，鞠躬三，舞蹈。

translations.literal: Announce inserting tablets, bow three times, perform ritual dance.
translations.idiomatic: They were called to insert their tablets, bow three times, and perform the ritual dance.

sentences.zh: 贊跪唱山呼，百官拱手加額曰：「萬歲。

translations.literal: Announce kneeling and calling the mountain shout; all officials cup hands and touch forehead saying: "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: They were called to kneel and perform the mountain shout; all officials cupped their hands and touched their foreheads, saying, "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 唱山呼，曰：「萬歲。

translations.literal: Call the mountain shout, saying: "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: The mountain shout was called again: "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 唱再山呼，曰：「萬萬歲」。

translations.literal: Call the mountain shout again, saying: "Ten thousand times ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: The mountain shout was called a second time: "Long live the emperor for ten thousand ages!"

sentences.zh: 凡呼萬歲，樂工軍校齊聲應之。

translations.literal: Whenever "ten thousand years" is called, musicians and military officers respond in unison.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever "Long live the emperor!" was shouted, musicians and military officers responded in unison.

sentences.zh: 贊出笏，俯伏，興，樂作。

translations.literal: Announce withdrawing tablets, prostrate, rise, music plays.
translations.idiomatic: They were called to withdraw their tablets, prostrate themselves, and rise as music played.

sentences.zh: 贊四拜，興，樂止。

translations.literal: Announce four bows, rise, music stops.
translations.idiomatic: Four final bows were announced; they rose, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 儀禮司奏禮畢，中和樂作。

translations.literal: The Ceremonial Protocol Office reports the rite is finished, the Harmonious Music plays.
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonial Protocol Office announced that the rite was finished, and the Harmonious Music began to play.

sentences.zh: 鳴鞭，駕興。

translations.literal: Crack the whip, the imperial carriage rises.
translations.idiomatic: The whip was cracked, and the imperial carriage set out.

sentences.zh: 尚寶官捧寶，導駕官前導，至華蓋殿，樂止。

translations.literal: The imperial seal official bears the seal, guiding officials lead ahead, reach the Hall of Imperial Canopy, music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial seal official bore the seal as guiding officials led the way to the Hall of Imperial Canopy, where the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 百官以次出。

translations.literal: All officials exit in order.
translations.idiomatic: All officials departed in turn.

sentences.zh: 洪武三十年，更定同文、玉帛案俱進安殿中，宣表訖，舉置於寶案之南。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Hongwu, it was revised that both the Shared Script and Jade-Silk tables enter and are placed in the hall, and after proclamation is finished are raised and placed south of the seal table.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of the Hongwu reign, it was revised so that both the Shared Script and Jade-Silk tables were brought into the hall; after the memorial was proclaimed, they were raised and placed south of the seal table.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十六年，更定蕃國貢方物案入于丹陛中道左右，設定時鼓於文樓上，大樂陳奉天門內東西，北向。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiajing, it was revised that the foreign tribute goods table enters on the left and right of the central path of the red steps, the timekeeping drum is set on the Civil Tower, great music is displayed east and west inside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of the Jiajing reign, it was revised so that the table for foreign tribute goods was placed on either side of the central path on the red steps, the timekeeping drum was set on the Civil Tower, and the great music ensemble was positioned east and west inside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, facing north.

sentences.zh: 他儀亦略有增損。

translations.literal: Other ceremonies also had slight additions and reductions.
translations.idiomatic: Other ceremonies were likewise subject to minor additions and reductions.

sentences.zh: 立春日進春，都城府縣舉春案由東階升，跪置於丹陛中道，俯伏，興。

translations.literal: On the day of the Beginning of Spring, spring is presented; the capital prefecture and counties raise the spring table up the east steps, kneel and place it on the central path of the red steps, prostrate and rise.
translations.idiomatic: On the Beginning of Spring, the spring offering was presented; officials of the capital prefecture and counties raised the spring table up the east steps, knelt to place it on the central path of the red steps, then prostrated themselves and rose.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，樂作。

translations.literal: Announce bow, music plays.
translations.idiomatic: Bows were announced, and music played.

sentences.zh: 四拜，興，樂止。

translations.literal: Four bows, rise, music stops.
translations.idiomatic: They performed four bows and rose, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 文武官北向立，致詞官詣中道之東，跪奏云：「新春吉辰，禮當慶賀。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials stand facing north; the speech-offering official proceeds to the east of the central path, kneels and reports saying: "On this auspicious day of the new spring, ritual requires congratulation."
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials stood facing north; the speech-offering official proceeded to the east of the central path, knelt, and reported: "On this auspicious day of the new spring, it is fitting to offer congratulations."

sentences.zh: 」贊拜，樂作。

translations.literal: " Announce bow, music plays.
translations.idiomatic: " Bows were announced, and music played.

sentences.zh: 五拜三叩頭，興，樂止。

translations.literal: Five bows and three prostrations, rise, music stops.
translations.idiomatic: They performed five bows and three prostrations, rose, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 儀禮司奏禮畢。

translations.literal: The Ceremonial Protocol Office reports the rite is finished.
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonial Protocol Office announced that the rite was finished.

sentences.zh: 正統十一年，正旦立春，禮部議順天府官進春後，百官即詣班行賀正旦禮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhengtong, when New Year's Day coincided with the Beginning of Spring, the Ministry of Rites deliberated that after Shuntian Prefecture officials presented spring, all officials should immediately proceed to their ranks to perform the New Year's congratulation rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Zhengtong reign, when New Year's Day fell on the same day as the Beginning of Spring, the Ministry of Rites ruled that after Shuntian Prefecture officials presented the spring offering, all officials should immediately take their places to perform the New Year's congratulation rite.

sentences.zh: 舊制，冬至日行賀禮。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations, congratulation rites were performed on the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, congratulation rites were performed on the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，分祀二郊，以冬至大報，是日行慶成禮。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiajing, the two suburban sacrifices were separated; the winter solstice became the great report, and on that day the celebration-of-completion rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Jiajing reign, the two suburban sacrifices were separated, and the winter solstice became the occasion for the great report to Heaven; on that day the celebration-of-completion rite was performed instead.

sentences.zh: 次日，帝詣內殿，行節祭禮。

translations.literal: The next day, the emperor proceeds to the inner hall and performs the seasonal sacrifice rite.
translations.idiomatic: The following day, the emperor proceeded to the inner hall to perform the seasonal sacrifice rite.

sentences.zh: 又詣母后前行賀禮訖，始御奉天殿受賀。

translations.literal: Also proceeds before the empress dowager to perform congratulation rites, and only then takes seat at the Hall of Supreme Harmony to receive congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: He also proceeded before the empress dowager to perform congratulation rites, and only then took his seat in the Hall of Supreme Harmony to receive congratulations from the officials.

sentences.zh: 常朝儀

translations.literal: Regular Audience Rite
translations.idiomatic: The Regular Audience Rite

sentences.zh: 古禮，天子有外朝、內朝、燕朝。

translations.literal: In ancient rites, the Son of Heaven had the outer court, inner court, and leisure court.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient ritual, the Son of Heaven held court in three settings: the outer court, the inner court, and the leisure court.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝五日一朝。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han held court once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han held court once every five days.

sentences.zh: 唐制，天子日御紫宸殿見羣臣曰常參，朔望御宣政殿見羣臣曰入閣。

translations.literal: Under the Tang system, when the Son of Heaven daily took the Purple Forbidden Hall to see his ministers it was called regular attendance; on the first and fifteenth he took the Xuanzheng Hall to see his ministers, called entering the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang system, when the emperor daily received his ministers in the Purple Forbidden Hall it was called regular attendance; on the first and fifteenth of the month, when he received them in the Xuanzheng Hall, it was called entering the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 宋則侍從官日朝垂拱謂之常參，百司五日一朝紫宸爲六參，在京朝官朔望朝紫宸爲朔參、望參。

translations.literal: In the Song, attendant officials daily attending at the Chui Gong Hall was called regular attendance; the hundred offices attending the Purple Forbidden Hall every five days was the six attendances; capital officials attending the Purple Forbidden Hall on the first and fifteenth was first-of-month attendance and mid-month attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the Song dynasty, when attendant officials attended daily at the Chui Gong Hall it was called regular attendance; when the hundred offices attended at the Purple Forbidden Hall every five days it was called the six attendances; and when capital officials attended at the Purple Forbidden Hall on the first and fifteenth of the month it was called first-of-month attendance and mid-month attendance.

sentences.zh: 明洪武三年定制，朔望日，帝皮弁服御奉天殿，百官朝服於丹墀東西，再拜。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu the Ming regulations were established: on the first and fifteenth, the emperor in the leather cap and court robe takes the Hall of Supreme Harmony; all officials in court dress on the east and west of the red courtyard perform two bows.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Hongwu reign, Ming regulations were established: on the first and fifteenth of each month, the emperor in leather cap and court robe took his seat in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, and all officials in court dress on the east and west sides of the red courtyard performed two bows.

sentences.zh: 班首詣前，同百官鞠躬，稱「聖躬萬福」。

translations.literal: The rank leader advances forward, together with all officials bows, and says "May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings."
translations.idiomatic: The leader of the ranks advanced, and together with all officials bowed and said, "May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings."

sentences.zh: 復位，皆再拜，分班對立。

translations.literal: Return to position, all bow twice again, divide into ranks and stand facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: They returned to their positions, all bowed twice again, and divided into ranks standing opposite one another.

sentences.zh: 省府臺部官有奏，由西階升殿。

translations.literal: If provincial, prefectural, censorial, or ministry officials have memorials to present, they ascend the hall by the west steps.
translations.idiomatic: If provincial, prefectural, censorial, or ministry officials had business to report, they ascended the hall by the west steps.

sentences.zh: 奏畢降階，百官出。

translations.literal: When presentation is finished descend the steps, all officials exit.
translations.idiomatic: When the presentations were finished they descended the steps, and all officials departed.

sentences.zh: 十七年，罷朔望起居禮。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the first-and-fifteenth attendance rite was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, the first-and-fifteenth attendance rite was abolished.

sentences.zh: 後更定，朔望御奉天殿，常朝官序立丹墀，東西向，謝恩見辭官序立奉天門外，北向。

translations.literal: Later it was revised: on the first and fifteenth the emperor takes the Hall of Supreme Harmony; regular audience officials stand in order on the red courtyard facing east or west; officials offering thanks or farewells stand in order outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony facing north.
translations.idiomatic: It was later revised so that on the first and fifteenth the emperor took the Hall of Supreme Harmony; officials of the regular audience stood in order on the red courtyard facing east or west; and officials offering thanks or taking leave stood in order outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony facing north.

sentences.zh: 升座作樂。

translations.literal: Ascend the throne, music plays.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the throne, and music played.

sentences.zh: 常朝官一拜三叩頭，樂止，復班。

translations.literal: Regular audience officials perform one bow and three prostrations, music stops, return to ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Regular audience officials performed one bow and three prostrations; the music ceased, and they returned to their ranks.

sentences.zh: 謝恩見辭官序立奉天門外，北向。

translations.literal: Officials offering thanks or farewells stand in order outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Officials offering thanks or taking leave stood in order outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, facing north.

sentences.zh: 升座作樂。

translations.literal: Ascend the throne, music plays.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the throne, and music played.

sentences.zh: 常朝官一拜三叩頭，樂止，復班。

translations.literal: Regular audience officials perform one bow and three prostrations, music stops, return to ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Regular audience officials performed one bow and three prostrations; the music ceased, and they returned to their ranks.

sentences.zh: 謝恩見辭官於奉天門外，五拜三叩頭畢，駕興。

translations.literal: Officials offering thanks or farewells outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, when five bows and three prostrations are finished, the imperial carriage rises.
translations.idiomatic: When officials offering thanks or taking leave outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony had finished five bows and three prostrations, the imperial carriage set out.

sentences.zh: 又凡早朝，御華蓋殿，文武官於鹿頂外東西立，鳴鞭，以次行禮訖。

translations.literal: Moreover for all morning audiences, the emperor takes the Hall of Imperial Canopy; civil and military officials stand east and west outside the Deer Crest; the whip is cracked; they perform the rite in order until finished.
translations.idiomatic: For all morning audiences, the emperor took the Hall of Imperial Canopy; civil and military officials stood to the east and west outside the Deer Crest; the whip was cracked, and they performed the rites in order until finished.

sentences.zh: 四品以上官入侍殿內，五品以下仍前北向立。

translations.literal: Officials of the fourth rank and above enter to attend inside the hall; fifth rank and below remain as before standing facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the fourth rank and above entered to attend inside the hall; those of the fifth rank and below remained where they were, standing facing north.

sentences.zh: 有事奏者出班，奏畢，鳴鞭以次出。

translations.literal: Those with business to present step out of rank; when presentation is finished, the whip is cracked and they exit in order.
translations.idiomatic: Those with business to report stepped out of rank; when they had finished, the whip was cracked and they departed in order.

sentences.zh: 如御奉天殿，先於華蓋殿行禮。

translations.literal: If taking the Hall of Supreme Harmony, first perform the rite at the Hall of Imperial Canopy.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor was to take the Hall of Supreme Harmony, the rites were first performed at the Hall of Imperial Canopy.

sentences.zh: 奏事畢，五品以下詣丹墀，北向立，五品以上及翰林院、給事中、御史於中左、中右門候鳴鞭，詣殿內序立，朝退出。

translations.literal: When presentations are finished, fifth rank and below proceed to the red courtyard and stand facing north; fifth rank and above and the Hanlin Academy, supervising secretaries, and censors wait at the central left and central right gates for the whip crack, proceed inside the hall to stand in order, and withdraw after the audience.
translations.idiomatic: When presentations were finished, officials of the fifth rank and below proceeded to the red courtyard and stood facing north; those of the fifth rank and above, together with members of the Hanlin Academy, supervising secretaries, and censors, waited at the central left and central right gates for the whip crack, then entered the hall to take their places in order and withdrew after the audience.

sentences.zh: 凡百官於御前侍坐，有官奏事，必起立，奏畢復坐。

translations.literal: Whenever all officials are seated in attendance before the emperor, if an official presents business he must stand, and when finished sit again.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever officials were seated in attendance before the emperor, any official who had business to present had to stand; when finished, he sat down again.

sentences.zh: 后皇帝行丹墀，常北面，不南向，左右周旋不背北。

translations.literal: When the emperor walks on the red courtyard, he usually faces north, not south; when turning left or right he does not turn his back to the north.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor walked on the red courtyard, he usually faced north rather than south, and when turning left or right he did not turn his back to the north.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升奉天門及丹陛，隨從官不得徑由中道並王道。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascends the Gate of Supreme Harmony and the red steps, attendant officials may not go directly by the central path or the imperial path.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended the Gate of Supreme Harmony and the red steps, attendant officials were forbidden to use the central path or the imperial path.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，定侍班官：東則六部都察院堂上官、十三道掌印御史、通政司、大理寺、太常寺、太僕寺、應天府、翰林院、春坊、光祿寺、欽天監、尚寶司、太醫院、五軍斷事及京縣官，西則五軍都督、錦衣衛指揮、各衛掌印指揮、給事中、中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, attendance officials were fixed: on the east—the six ministries, censorate chief officials, thirteen circuit chief censors, Office of Transmission, Court of Judicial Review, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Court of the Imperial Stud, Yingtian Prefecture, Hanlin Academy, Eastern Palace, Court of Imperial Entertainments, Directorate of Astronomy, Imperial Seals Office, Imperial Medical Academy, Five Armies judicial officers, and capital county officials; on the west—the Five Armies commanders, Embroidered Uniform Guard commanders, guard circuit chief commanders, supervising secretaries, and secretarial draftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, the officials who attended court were fixed: on the east were chief officials of the six ministries and censorate, chief censors of the thirteen circuits, the Office of Transmission, Court of Judicial Review, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Court of the Imperial Stud, Yingtian Prefecture, Hanlin Academy, Eastern Palace, Court of Imperial Entertainments, Directorate of Astronomy, Imperial Seals Office, Imperial Medical Academy, Five Armies judicial officers, and capital county officials; on the west were commanders of the Five Armies, Embroidered Uniform Guard, and guard circuits, supervising secretaries, and secretarial draftsmen.

sentences.zh: 又令禮部置百官朝牌，大書品級，列丹墀左右木柵上，依序立。

translations.literal: Also ordered the Ministry of Rites to set up officials' audience placards, writing ranks in large characters, arrayed on the wooden railings left and right of the red courtyard, standing in order.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites was also ordered to prepare audience placards for all officials, with ranks written in large characters and posted on the wooden railings to the left and right of the red courtyard, so that officials could stand in their proper order.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，令凡入殿必履鞋。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, it was ordered that all who enter the hall must wear shoes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, it was ordered that all who entered the hall must wear shoes.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，令內閣官侍朝立金臺東，錦衣衛在西，後移御道，東西對立。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, it was ordered that Grand Secretariat officials attending court stand east of the Golden Terrace, the Embroidered Uniform Guard on the west; later moved to the imperial path, standing opposite east and west.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongle reign, Grand Secretariat officials attending court were ordered to stand east of the Golden Terrace and the Embroidered Uniform Guard on the west; later they were moved to the imperial path, standing opposite one another east and west.

sentences.zh: 四年諭六部及近侍官曰：「早朝多四方所奏事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he instructed the six ministries and close attendant officials, saying: "The morning audience mostly involves matters reported from the four directions."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he instructed the six ministries and close attendant officials: "The morning audience is mostly taken up with reports from the provinces."

sentences.zh: 午後事簡，君臣之間得從容陳論。

translations.literal: Afternoon business is simpler; between ruler and ministers one can discuss at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Afternoon business is lighter, and ruler and ministers can discuss matters at greater leisure.

sentences.zh: 自今有事當商榷者，皆於晚朝。

translations.literal: From now on, matters that should be deliberated are all at the evening audience.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, all matters requiring deliberation shall be taken up at the evening audience.

sentences.zh: 」四年，諭行在禮部曰：「北京冬氣嚴凝，羣臣早朝奏事，立久不勝。

translations.literal: " In the fourth year he instructed the traveling Ministry of Rites, saying: "Beijing's winter air is severely cold; when the multitude of ministers present business at the morning audience, standing long they cannot endure it."
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth year he instructed the traveling Ministry of Rites: "Beijing's winter cold is severe; when ministers present business at the morning audience, they cannot endure standing so long."

sentences.zh: 今後朝畢，於右順門內便殿奏事。」

translations.literal: From now on after the audience is finished, present business in the convenient hall inside the Right Shun Gate."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, after the audience is finished, business shall be presented in the convenient hall inside the Right Shun Gate."

sentences.zh: 景泰初，定午朝儀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai, the midday audience rite was established.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign, the midday audience rite was established.

sentences.zh: 凡午朝，御左順門，設寶案。

translations.literal: For all midday audiences, take the Left Shun Gate, set out the seal table.
translations.idiomatic: For all midday audiences, the emperor took the Left Shun Gate and the seal table was set out.

sentences.zh: 執事奏事官候於左掖門外。

translations.literal: Officiating officials who present business wait outside the left side gate.
translations.idiomatic: Officiating officials who had business to present waited outside the left side gate.

sentences.zh: 駕出，以次入。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage exits, enter in order.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage set out, and officials entered in order.

sentences.zh: 內閣、五府、六部奏事官，六科侍班官，案西序立；

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat, Five Offices, and six ministries memorial-presenting officials, six offices attendance officials, stand in western order by the table;
translations.idiomatic: Memorial-presenting officials of the Grand Secretariat, Five Offices, and six ministries, together with attendance officials of the six offices, stood in western order by the table;

sentences.zh: 侍班御史二，序班二，將軍四，案南面北立；

translations.literal: two attendance censors, two rank-order ushers, four generals, south of the table facing north;
translations.idiomatic: two attendance censors, two rank-order ushers, and four generals stood south of the table, facing north;

sentences.zh: 鳴贊一，案東，西向立；

translations.literal: one announcer, east of the table, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: one announcer stood east of the table, facing west;

sentences.zh: 錦衣衛、鴻臚寺東向立；

translations.literal: Embroidered Uniform Guard and Court of State Ceremonial stand facing east;
translations.idiomatic: the Embroidered Uniform Guard and Court of State Ceremonial stood facing east;

sentences.zh: 管將軍官、侍衛官立於將軍西。

translations.literal: commanding generals and guard officials stand west of the generals.
translations.idiomatic: commanding generals and guard officials stood to the west of the generals.

sentences.zh: 府部奏事畢，撤案，各官退。

translations.literal: When ministry presentations are finished, remove the table, all officials withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministries had finished presenting business, the table was removed and all officials withdrew.

sentences.zh: 有密事，赴御前奏。

translations.literal: If there are confidential matters, proceed before the emperor to present them.
translations.idiomatic: If there were confidential matters, officials proceeded before the emperor to present them.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，令常朝官禮畢，內閣官由東陛、錦衣衛官由西陛升，立於寶座東西。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiajing, it was ordered that when regular audience officials finish the rite, Grand Secretariat officials ascend by the east steps and Embroidered Uniform Guard officials by the west steps, standing east and west of the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Jiajing reign, it was ordered that after regular audience officials finished their rites, Grand Secretariat officials should ascend by the east steps and Embroidered Uniform Guard officials by the west steps, standing to the east and west of the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 有欽差官及外國人領敕，坊局官一人奉敕立內閣後，稍上，候領敕官辭，奉敕官承旨由左陛下，循御道授之。

translations.literal: If there are imperial commissioners or foreigners receiving edicts, one workshop official bearing the edict stands behind the Grand Secretariat, slightly higher, waits until the edict-receiving official takes leave; the edict-bearing official receives the decree and by the left steps, following the imperial path, bestows it.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial commissioners or foreigners came to receive edicts, one workshop official bearing the edict stood behind the Grand Secretariat, slightly elevated; when the recipient had taken leave, the edict-bearing official received the decree and, descending the left steps along the imperial path, bestowed it.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年，詔以三六九日視朝。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Longqing, an edict ordered holding court on the third, sixth, and ninth days.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Longqing reign, an edict ordered that the emperor hold court on the third, sixth, and ninth days of each month.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三年，令常朝日記注起居官四人，列於東班給事中上，稍前，以便觀聽。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wanli, it was ordered that on regular audience days four diarist attendance officials be arrayed above the eastern-rank supervising secretaries, slightly forward, for convenient observation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Wanli reign, four diarist attendance officials were ordered to stand above the eastern-rank supervising secretaries on regular audience days, slightly forward, so they could observe and record proceedings.

sentences.zh: 午朝，則列於御座西，稍南。

translations.literal: At the midday audience, they are arrayed west of the imperial throne, slightly south.
translations.idiomatic: At the midday audience, they stood west of the imperial throne, slightly to the south.

sentences.zh: 凡入朝次第，洪武二十四年，令朝參將軍先入，近侍次之，公、侯、駙馬、伯又次之，五府、六部又次之，應天府及在京雜職官員又次之。

translations.literal: For all order of entering court, in the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu it was ordered: attendance generals enter first, close attendants next, dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, and earls next, the five offices and six ministries next, Yingtian Prefecture and miscellaneous capital officials last.
translations.idiomatic: The order of entering court was fixed in the twenty-fourth year of the Hongwu reign: attendance generals entered first, then close attendants, then dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, and earls, then the five offices and six ministries, and finally Yingtian Prefecture and miscellaneous capital officials.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年令進士照辦事衙門次第，立見任官後。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua it was ordered that metropolitan graduates follow the order of their assigned yamen and stand after incumbent officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of the Chenghua reign, metropolitan graduates were ordered to follow the ranking of their assigned offices and stand behind incumbent officials.

sentences.zh: 皇太子親王朝儀

translations.literal: Crown Prince's Personal Audience Rite
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's Personal Audience Rite

sentences.zh: 二十六年，改定朝賀於乾清宮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, court congratulations were revised to be held at the Palace of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, court congratulations were moved to the Palace of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 其日，皇帝、皇后升座，侍從導引如儀，引禮引皇太子及妃、親王及妃詣上位前，贊禮贊四拜，興。

translations.literal: On that day, the emperor and empress ascend their thrones, attendants guide as prescribed; the usher leads the crown prince and consort, princes and consorts before the upper seat; the ritual announcer announces four bows, rise.
translations.idiomatic: On that day, the emperor and empress ascended their thrones with attendants guiding as prescribed; ushers led the crown prince and his consort and the princes and their consorts before the imperial seats; four bows were announced, and they rose.

sentences.zh: 贊禮引皇太子詣前，贊跪，引禮讚太了妃、諸王及妃皆跪。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer leads the crown prince forward, announces kneeling; the usher announces the crown princess consort, all princes and consorts kneel.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer led the crown prince forward and called for kneeling; the usher called for the crown princess consort and all princes and their consorts to kneel as well.

sentences.zh: 皇太子致詞，同前，不傳制。

translations.literal: The crown prince offers the speech, as before, no edict transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince delivered the congratulatory address as before, but no edict was transmitted.

sentences.zh: 贊禮贊皇太子俯伏，興，引禮讚諸王俯伏，興，太子妃、諸王妃皆興。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer announces the crown prince prostrates and rises; the usher announces all princes prostrate and rise; the crown princess and all princess consorts rise.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince prostrated himself and rose at the announcer's call; the princes did likewise; the crown princess and all princess consorts then rose.

sentences.zh: 贊禮引皇太子復位。

translations.literal: The ritual announcer leads the crown prince back to position.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual announcer led the crown prince back to his place.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，皇太子以下皆四拜。

translations.literal: Announce bow; the crown prince and below all perform four bows.
translations.idiomatic: Bows were announced, and the crown prince and all below him performed four bows.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，引禮引至皇后前，其前後贊拜，皆如朝皇帝儀。

translations.literal: When the rite is finished, the usher leads them before the empress; the bows before and after are all as in audience with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, they were led before the empress, and the bows before and after were performed just as in audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 致詞稱「母后殿下」。

translations.literal: The speech addresses "Mother Empress Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: The address referred to her as "Mother Empress Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 禮畢，出。

translations.literal: When the rite is finished, exit.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, they departed.

sentences.zh: 七年更定，不致賀辭，止行八拜禮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year it was revised: no congratulatory speech, only eight bows performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year it was revised so that no congratulatory speech was offered and only eight bows were performed.

sentences.zh: 朝賀皇太后禮皆同。

translations.literal: Congratulations to the empress dowager follow the same rite.
translations.idiomatic: Congratulations to the empress dowager followed the same rite.

sentences.zh: 諸王來朝儀

translations.literal: Princes' Coming-to-Court Rite
translations.idiomatic: The Princes' Coming-to-Court Rite

sentences.zh: 古者，六年五服一朝。

translations.literal: In antiquity, once every six years within the five degrees of mourning dress there was one court audience.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, princes came to court once every six years, within the cycle of the five degrees of mourning relationship.

sentences.zh: 漢法有四見儀。

translations.literal: Han law had four audience ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Han law prescribed four forms of audience ceremony.

sentences.zh: 魏制，籓王不得入覲。

translations.literal: Under Wei regulations, feudatory princes were not permitted to enter for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei regulations, feudatory princes were not permitted to come to court for audience.

sentences.zh: 晉泰始中，令王公以下入朝者，四方各爲二番。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era of Jin, those entering court from the four directions, from princes and dukes downward, were each divided into two rotations.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era of Jin, those coming to court from the four directions—from princes and dukes downward—were each divided into two rotations.

sentences.zh: 唐以後，親籓多不就國。

translations.literal: After the Tang, imperial princedoms mostly did not go to their fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang, imperial princes mostly did not take up residence in their assigned fiefs.

sentences.zh: 明代仿古封建，親王之籓不常入朝，朝則賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: The Ming modeled ancient feudal enfeoffment; princes at their fiefs did not often come to court, but when they did the gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming modeled the ancient system of feudal enfeoffment; princes in their fiefs did not often come to court, but when they did the gifts bestowed were exceedingly generous.

sentences.zh: 明初，凡來朝，先期陳御座於奉天殿，如常儀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming, for all coming to court, the imperial throne was set out in advance at the Hall of Supreme Harmony, as in the regular rite.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Ming, whenever princes came to court, the imperial throne was set out in advance at the Hall of Supreme Harmony, following the regular ceremony.

sentences.zh: 諸王次於奉天門外東耳房。

translations.literal: The princes wait in the eastern side chamber outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The princes waited in the eastern side chamber outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 鼓三嚴，百官入就侍立位。

translations.literal: At the third drum signal, all officials enter and take their attendance positions.
translations.idiomatic: At the third drum signal, all officials entered and took their attendance positions.

sentences.zh: 引禮導王具袞冕，由東門入，升東陛，就位。

translations.literal: The usher leads the prince in full regalia, entering through the east gate, ascending the east steps, and taking position.
translations.idiomatic: The usher led the prince in full regalia through the east gate, up the east steps, to his position.

sentences.zh: 王府從官就丹墀位。

translations.literal: The prince's entourage take their positions on the red courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's entourage took their positions on the red courtyard.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，樂作，王與從官皆四拜。

translations.literal: Announce bow, music plays, the prince and entourage all perform four bows.
translations.idiomatic: Bows were announced; music played, and the prince and his entourage all performed four bows.

sentences.zh: 興，樂止。

translations.literal: Rise, music stops.
translations.idiomatic: They rose, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 王從殿東門入，樂作。

translations.literal: The prince enters through the hall's east gate, music plays.
translations.idiomatic: The prince entered through the hall's east gate as music played.

sentences.zh: 內贊導至御前，樂止。

translations.literal: The inner announcer guides him before the emperor, music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The inner announcer guided him before the emperor, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 王跪，王府官皆跪。

translations.literal: The prince kneels, all prince's mansion officials kneel.
translations.idiomatic: The prince knelt, and all officials of his princely establishment knelt as well.

sentences.zh: 王致辭曰：「第幾子某王某，茲遇某時入覲，欽詣父皇陛下朝拜。

translations.literal: The prince offers speech, saying: "The such-and-such son Prince So-and-so, on this occasion of entering for audience at such-and-such time, respectfully proceeds before Father Emperor Your Majesty to perform obeisance."
translations.idiomatic: The prince delivered his address: "Your son, the such-and-such Prince So-and-so, having come to court on this occasion, respectfully proceeds before Father Emperor Your Majesty to perform obeisance."

sentences.zh: 」贊俯伏，興。

translations.literal: " Announce prostrate, rise.
translations.idiomatic: " He was called to prostrate himself and then rise.

sentences.zh: 王由東門出。

translations.literal: The prince exits through the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: The prince exited through the east gate.

sentences.zh: 樂作，復拜位，樂止。

translations.literal: Music plays, return to bowing position, music stops.
translations.idiomatic: Music played as he returned to the bowing position, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，王興。

translations.literal: Announce bow, the prince rises.
translations.idiomatic: Bows were announced, and the prince rose.

sentences.zh: 從官皆四拜，興。
