translations.literal: The officials bearing the booklet and seal placed them in the carriage; inner attendants raised the carriage; the emperor followed the carriage, descended the steps, and mounted the imperial chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The officials bearing the booklet and seal placed them in the carriage; inner attendants raised the carriage, and the emperor followed it, descended the steps, and mounted the imperial chariot.

sentences.zh: 百官於金水橋南，北向立，輿至皆跪，過興。

translations.literal: All officials stood south of the Golden Water Bridge facing north; when the carriage arrived all knelt; when it passed they rose.
translations.idiomatic: All officials stood south of the Golden Water Bridge facing north; when the carriage arrived they all knelt, and when it passed they rose.

sentences.zh: 隨至思善門外橋南，北向立。

translations.literal: They followed to south of the bridge outside the Gate of Cherishing Virtue and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: They followed to south of the bridge outside the Gate of Cherishing Virtue and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 皇帝至思善門內降輅。

translations.literal: The emperor reached inside the Gate of Cherishing Virtue and descended from the chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reached inside the Gate of Cherishing Virtue and descended from the chariot.

sentences.zh: 皇太后升座。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ascended to her seat.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ascended to her seat.

sentences.zh: 輿至丹陛。

translations.literal: The carriage reached the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage reached the red steps.

sentences.zh: 皇帝由左門入，至陛右，北向立。

translations.literal: The emperor entered through the left gate, reached the right of the steps, and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered through the left gate, proceeded to the right of the steps, and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 親王冕服各就位。

translations.literal: The princes in full regalia each took their positions.
translations.idiomatic: The princes in full regalia each took their positions.

sentences.zh: 奏四拜，皇帝及王以下皆四拜。

translations.literal: Four bows were announced; the emperor and all below the princes performed four bows.
translations.idiomatic: Four bows were announced; the emperor and all below the princes performed four bows.

sentences.zh: 奉冊寶官以冊寶由殿中門入，立於左。

translations.literal: The officials bearing the booklet and seal entered through the central gate of the hall and stood to the left.
translations.idiomatic: The officials bearing the booklet and seal entered through the central gate of the hall and stood to the left.

sentences.zh: 皇帝由殿左門入，至拜位跪，親王百官皆跪。

translations.literal: The emperor entered through the left gate of the hall, reached the bowing position and knelt; princes and all officials knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered through the left gate of the hall, proceeded to the bowing position and knelt, and the princes and all officials knelt as well.

sentences.zh: 奏搢圭，奏進冊。

translations.literal: Report inserting the tablet, report presenting the investiture document.
translations.idiomatic: It was announced that the tablet should be inserted, then that the investiture document should be presented.

sentences.zh: 奉冊官以冊跪進，皇帝受冊獻訖，執事官跪受，置案左。

translations.literal: The document-bearing official kneels and presents the investiture document; the emperor receives it and the presentation is finished; the officiating official kneels to receive it and places it on the left of the table.
translations.idiomatic: The document-bearing official knelt and presented the investiture document; the emperor received it, and when the presentation was finished, an officiating official knelt to receive it and placed it on the left side of the table.

sentences.zh: 奏進寶，奉寶官以寶跪進。

translations.literal: Report presenting the seal; the seal-bearing official kneels and presents the seal.
translations.idiomatic: It was announced that the seal should be presented, and the seal-bearing official knelt to present it.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受寶，獻訖，執事官跪受，置案右。

translations.literal: The emperor receives the seal, the presentation is finished, the officiating official kneels to receive it and places it on the right of the table.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the seal, and when the presentation was finished, an officiating official knelt to receive it and placed it on the right side of the table.

sentences.zh: 奏出圭，奏宣冊，執事官跪宣讀。

translations.literal: Report withdrawing the tablet, report proclaiming the investiture document; the officiating official kneels and reads it aloud.
translations.idiomatic: It was announced that the tablet should be withdrawn and the investiture document proclaimed; an officiating official knelt and read it aloud.

sentences.zh: 皇帝俯伏，興，由左門出，至拜位。

translations.literal: The emperor prostrates himself and rises, exits through the left gate, and reaches the bowing position.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor prostrated himself and rose, then exited through the left gate to the bowing position.

sentences.zh: 奏四拜，傳唱百官同四拜。

translations.literal: Report four bows; the announcement is transmitted and all officials likewise perform four bows.
translations.idiomatic: Four bows were announced, and the call was transmitted so that all officials performed four bows as well.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，駕興。

translations.literal: When the rite is finished, the imperial carriage rises.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, the imperial carriage set out.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇帝奉皇太后謁奉先殿及几筵，行謁謝禮。

translations.literal: On that day, the emperor leads the empress dowager to visit the Hall of Imperial Ancestors and the spirit tablet, performing the rite of thanksgiving visit.
translations.idiomatic: On that day, the emperor led the empress dowager to visit the Hall of Imperial Ancestors and the spirit tablet to perform the thanksgiving visit rite.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，皇太后還宮，服燕居冠服，升座。

translations.literal: When the rite is finished, the empress dowager returns to the palace, dons leisure crown and robes, and ascends the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, the empress dowager returned to the palace, dressed in her leisure crown and robes, and ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 皇帝率皇后、皇妃、親王、公主及六尚等女官行慶賀禮。

translations.literal: The emperor leads the empress, imperial consorts, princes, princesses, and female officials of the six inner bureaus in performing congratulation rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led the empress, imperial consorts, princes, princesses, and female officials of the six inner bureaus in performing congratulation rites.

sentences.zh: 翌日，外命婦四品以上行進表箋禮。

translations.literal: The next day, external titled ladies of the fourth rank and above perform the rite of presenting memorials and petitions.
translations.idiomatic: The following day, external titled ladies of the fourth rank and above performed the rite of presenting memorials and petitions.

sentences.zh: 宣德以後，儀同。

translations.literal: From the Xuande reign onward, the rite was the same.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xuande reign onward, the ceremony followed the same form.

sentences.zh: 正統初，尊太皇太后儀同。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong, honoring the grand empress dowager followed the same rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengtong reign, honoring the grand empress dowager followed the same ceremony.

sentences.zh: 天順八年二月，增命婦致詞云：「某夫人妾某氏等，恭惟皇太后陛下尊居慈極，永膺福壽。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year of Tianshun, the titled ladies' speech was augmented, saying: "Lady So-and-so, your concubines So-and-so and others, respectfully considering Her Majesty the Empress Dowager dwelling in the utmost of compassion, may forever receive blessings and longevity."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year of the Tianshun reign, the titled ladies' address was expanded to read: "Lady So-and-so, your concubines So-and-so and others respectfully consider that Her Majesty the Empress Dowager dwells in the utmost seat of compassion and may forever receive blessings and long life."

sentences.zh: 」弘治十八年，上兩宮尊號，改皇太后致詞云：「尊居慈闈，茂隆福壽。」

translations.literal: " In the eighteenth year of Hongzhi, honorific titles were bestowed on both palaces; the empress dowager's speech was changed to: "Dwelling in the compassionate inner quarters, may blessings and longevity flourish abundantly."
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighteenth year of the Hongzhi reign, honorific titles were bestowed on both palaces, and the empress dowager's address was changed to: "Dwelling in the compassionate inner quarters, may blessings and longevity flourish abundantly."

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年二月上尊號，以四宮行禮過勞，分爲二日。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Jiajing, when bestowing honorific titles, because performing rites at all four palaces was excessively taxing, it was divided into two days.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of the Jiajing reign, when honorific titles were bestowed, the ceremonies at all four palaces were found excessively taxing and were therefore divided over two days.

sentences.zh: 又以武宗服制未滿，莊肅皇后免朝賀，命婦賀三宮，亦分日。

translations.literal: Also because the mourning period for Emperor Wuzong had not yet been completed, Empress Zhuangsu was exempted from court congratulations; titled ladies congratulating the three palaces were also divided by day.
translations.idiomatic: Because the mourning period for Emperor Wuzong had not yet been completed, Empress Zhuangsu was exempted from court congratulations, and titled ladies offering congratulations at the three palaces were likewise scheduled on separate days.

sentences.zh: 上徽號，自天順二年正月奉皇太后始。

translations.literal: Bestowing commendatory epithets began in the first month of the second year of Tianshun, when honoring the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The bestowal of commendatory epithets began in the first month of the second year of the Tianshun reign, with the honoring of the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 致詞云：「嗣皇帝臣，伏惟皇太后陛下，功德兼隆，顯崇徽號，永膺福壽，率土同歡。

translations.literal: The speech says: "The succeeding emperor your subject, respectfully considering Her Majesty the Empress Dowager, whose merit and virtue are both lofty, may the commendatory epithet be gloriously elevated, may blessings and longevity be forever received, and all within the realm rejoice together."
translations.idiomatic: The address read: "The succeeding emperor, your subject, respectfully considers that Her Majesty the Empress Dowager's merit and virtue are both lofty; may her commendatory epithet be gloriously elevated, may she forever receive blessings and long life, and may all within the realm rejoice together."

sentences.zh: 」命婦進表慶賀致詞云：「某夫人妾某氏等，恭惟皇太后陛下德同坤厚，允協徽稱，壽福無疆，輿情歡戴。

translations.literal: " The titled ladies presenting memorials of congratulation offer speech, saying: "Lady So-and-so, your concubines So-and-so and others, respectfully considering Her Majesty the Empress Dowager, whose virtue matches the earth's thickness, fitting the commendatory designation, blessings and longevity without limit, the people's sentiment joyfully upholds her."
translations.idiomatic: " The titled ladies' congratulatory memorial address read: "Lady So-and-so, your concubines So-and-so and others respectfully consider that Her Majesty the Empress Dowager's virtue matches the earth in its depth, that it fittingly accords with her commendatory designation, that her blessings and longevity are without limit, and that the people's hearts rejoice to uphold her."

sentences.zh: 」餘如常儀。

translations.literal: " The remainder follows the regular ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: " The remainder followed the regular ceremony.

sentences.zh: 后上徽號及加上徽號，仿此。

translations.literal: When the empress receives a commendatory epithet or has one added, follow this model.
translations.idiomatic: When an empress received a commendatory epithet or had one added, the ceremony followed this model.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年，禮部具儀上，未及皇太子妃禮，特命增之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua, when the Ministry of Rites submitted the complete ceremony, it had not yet reached the crown princess consort's rite; a special order was issued to add it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of the Chenghua reign, when the Ministry of Rites submitted the complete ceremony, it did not yet include rites for the crown princess consort; a special order was issued to add them.
